## Summary A previous advisory (CVE-2026-49463 / GHSA-qpm9-h556-mwxm) reported that any logged-in user could download any document by its identifier, and stated this was fixed in 3.0.1. For the document-content part that fix was **incomplete**: documents remained downloadable by any authenticated user in 3.0.1 and 3.0.2, and the issue was only fully resolved in **3.0.3**. ## Relationship to CVE-2026-49463 This advisory is a follow-up to CVE-2026-49463. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-x96m-rh44-vgv8: Apache Shiro: LDAP DN Injection in DefaultLdapRealm
entry.content:
Apache Shiro: LDAP DN Injection in DefaultLdapRealm

Aliases: CVE-2026-49268

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/S:P/AU:Y/R:A/RE:L/U:Red

Affected:

  • org.apache.shiro:shiro-core — fixed in 2.2.1
  • org.apache.shiro:shiro-core — fixed in 3.0.0-alpha-2

A remote attacker can inject LDAP special characters into the Distinguished Name (DN) construction in DefaultLdapRealm class. User-supplied username input is directly concatenated into the LDAP DN template without any escaping of RFC 2253 special characters. This allows an attacker to manipulate the DN structure used for LDAP bind authentication, potentially bypassing authentication or impersonating other users. This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 2.2.0, and 3.0.0-alpha-1 when using DefaultLdapRealm Upgrade to Apache Shiro 2.2.1 or 3.0.0-alpha-2 or later, which fixes the issue.

Strimzi: Unrestricted access to all Secrets within namespace watched by the Topic operator

Aliases: CVE-2026-55226

Affected:

### Impact When only the Topic or only the User operators are deployed as part of the Entity Operator in the `Kafka` custom resource, the RBAC rights are not following the principle of least-privilege and the Entity Operator ServiceAccount still has access rights corresponding to both operators. That might allow the ServiceAccount to access `KafkaUser` custom resources and Secrets when the User operator is not deployed and access `KafkaTopic` custom resources when the Topic operator is not deployed. ### Patches The issue is fixed in Strimzi 1.0.1 and 1.1.0. ### Workarounds There is no workaround for this issue.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-2f55-g35j-5jmf: HAPI FHIR: XXE in XsltUtilities.saxonTransform via unhardened Saxon TransformerFactory
entry.content:
HAPI FHIR: XXE in XsltUtilities.saxonTransform via unhardened Saxon TransformerFactory

Aliases: CVE-2026-55471

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • ca.uhn.hapi.fhir:org.hl7.fhir.utilities — fixed in 6.9.10

### Summary `org.hl7.fhir.utilities.XsltUtilities` exposes two parallel families of XSLT transform helpers. The `transform(...)` overloads obtain their `TransformerFactory` from the project's hardened helper `XMLUtil.newXXEProtectedTransformerFactory()` (which sets `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD=""` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET=""`). The sibling `saxonTransform(...)` overloads instead instantiate a **bare** `new net.sf.saxon.TransformerFactoryImpl()` with no external-access restriction. A document transformed through any `saxonTransform(...)` overload is parsed with external general entities and external DTD/parameter entities enabled, so an attacker who controls (or can MITM) the transformed XML obtains XML External Entity injection: local file disclosure and blind XXE / SSRF to arbitrary URLs …

LangChain4j: SQL injection via metadata filters in langchain4j-mariadb and langchain4j-pgvector

Aliases: CVE-2026-55405

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:L

Affected:

  • dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-mariadb — fixed in 1.2.1-beta8
  • dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-mariadb — fixed in 1.5.1-beta11
  • dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-mariadb — fixed in 1.11.8-beta19
  • dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-mariadb — fixed in 1.16.3-beta26
  • dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-pgvector — fixed in 1.2.1-beta8
  • dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-pgvector — fixed in 1.5.1-beta11
  • dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-pgvector — fixed in 1.11.8-beta19
  • dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-pgvector — fixed in 1.16.3-beta26

### Summary The MariaDB and pgvector embedding stores build metadata-filter SQL by string-concatenating filter **keys** (and, in MariaDB, string **values**) directly into the query without adequate escaping. A crafted metadata key in `EmbeddingSearchRequest.filter()` can break out of its SQL context and inject arbitrary SQL into the statements executed by the stores' search and `removeAll(Filter)` operations. ### Details **pgvector — JSON mode (default, `COMBINED_JSON` / `COMBINED_JSONB`).** `JSONFilterMapper` places the key inside a single-quoted SQL literal (the JSON key of the `->>` operator) with no escaping: (metadata->>'<key>')::text A key containing a single quote breaks out, e.g. `metadataKey("')::text IS NOT NULL OR pg_sleep(1) IS NOT NULL --")` injects a live `pg_sleep(1)`…

References:

  • https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j/security/advisories/GHSA-2mfg-cc43-9pcj
  • https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j
